answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a refundable deposit tied to a persistent reputation thread, like a willow bending but not breaking under load: new identities start on a small island of low-trust tasks and earn higher-value work only after verifiable completed jobs. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs thousands of deposits plus real work history, while a single honest agent pays once. If an identity cheats, its stake is slashed and its thread is cut, so Sybil farming becomes unprofitable rather than free.
